title: Position picture-in-picture from its final size, like webcam overlay
author: ludagoo
body:
## What

Stock `default/hypr/apps/pip.lua` floats Chromium/Firefox PiP, forces `size = { 600, 338 }`, then parks it with:

```lua
move = { "(monitor_w-window_w-40)", "(monitor_h*0.04)" }
```

Hyprland evaluates `window_w` / `window_h` from the **client's original size**, then applies `size`. Chromium PiP often opens around 200px wide, so on a 1440-wide panel that becomes:

- x = 1440 − 200 − 40 = **1200**
- resize to 600px
- right edge at **1800** → **360px hanging off the right** (about half the overlay)

This is a kit-wide rule, but it is much more obvious on a lower-res older MacBook Air (this was reproduced on a 2015 Air, eDP-1 1440×900 @ 1x). On a 2560 or 4K display the same ~360px overflow is a small corner nibble that is easy to miss.

`default/hypr/apps/webcam-overlay.lua` already avoids this: it inlines the same size math in both `size` and `move` instead of using `window_w`. This PR copies that pattern for PiP and the Meet overlay.

```lua
move = { "(monitor_w-600-40)", "(monitor_h*0.04)" }
```

Verified on the same 1440×900 Air with a 200×112 GTK window titled `Picture-in-Picture`:

| | x | size | right edge | vs 1440 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before | 1200 | 600×338 | 1800 | 360px off |
| After | 800 | 600×338 | 1400 | 40px margin |

Y was already correct (`monitor_h*0.04`). Meet's bottom offset had the same `window_h` bug and is inlined to 338 to match.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash test/shell.d/pip-window-rules-test.sh`
- [x] 200px client under stock rules lands at x=1200 (360px off a 1440-wide Air)
- [x] 200px client with this move expression lands at x=800 (40px from the right)
- Pop a YouTube/Chromium PiP on a 1080p or 1440×900 panel: it should sit in the top-right with a 40px gap, not hang off the right
- Existing PiP windows do not re-run static move rules; close and re-open to pick this up

files.patch:
@@ -1,4 +1,8 @@
 -- Picture-in-picture overlays.
+-- Inline 600x338 in move the same way webcam-overlay.lua inlines its size
+-- expressions. Hyprland evaluates window_w / window_h from the client's
+-- original size, then applies size, so a small Chromium PiP would otherwise
+-- hang off the right edge.
 o.window({ title = "(Picture.?in.?[Pp]icture)" }, { tag = "+pip" })
 o.window({ tag = "pip" }, {
   tag = "-default-opacity",
@@ -8,7 +12,7 @@ o.window({ tag = "pip" }, {
   keep_aspect_ratio = true,
   border_size = 0,
   opacity = "1 1",
-  move = { "(monitor_w-window_w-40)", "(monitor_h*0.04)" },
+  move = { "(monitor_w-600-40)", "(monitor_h*0.04)" },
 })
 
 -- Google Meet PiP uses the meeting title instead of "Picture-in-Picture".
@@ -20,5 +24,5 @@ o.window({ tag = "chromium-based-browser", title = "^Meet - .+" }, {
   keep_aspect_ratio = true,
   border_size = 0,
   opacity = "1 1",
-  move = { "(monitor_w-window_w-40)", "(monitor_h-window_h-40)" },
+  move = { "(monitor_w-600-40)", "(monitor_h-338-40)" },
 })

@@ -0,0 +1,16 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
+
+pip="$ROOT/default/hypr/apps/pip.lua"
+
+if grep -E 'move = .*window_[wh]' "$pip" >/dev/null; then
+  fail "pip.lua move does not use window_w or window_h" "$(grep -n -E 'move = .*window_[wh]' "$pip")"
+fi
+
+grep -F '(monitor_w-600-40)' "$pip" >/dev/null || fail "pip.lua inlines 600 in the move x expression"
+grep -F '(monitor_h-338-40)' "$pip" >/dev/null || fail "Meet PiP inlines 338 in the move y expression"
+
+pass "pip.lua inlines size in move expressions like webcam-overlay.lua"
